# Question: generator shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **`top_left_tile`**: infer the global period
shape, but obtain each residue value only from the corresponding cell in the
top-left period block. It fits all three usable canonical demonstrations, because
none of their missing cells makes that particular readout disagree with the
selected rule.

An exact disagreement input is retained at
`repo/generators/54b040e4bd08/counterexamples/top_left_tile_input.json`:

```json
[
  [1,2,3,1,2,3,1,2,3],
  [4,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,6],
  [1,2,3,1,2,3,1,2,3],
  [4,5,6,4,5,6,4,5,6],
  [1,2,3,1,2,3,1,2,3],
  [4,5,6,4,5,6,4,5,6]
]
```

The intended output restores row 1 to `[4,5,6,4,5,6,4,5,6]`. The shortcut
instead reads zeros from the damaged top-left `2x3` block and produces
`[4,0,0,4,0,0,4,0,6]`, differing in five cells.

I checked the intended answer three ways: the input passes the final
`self_check`; an independent Python period oracle produced the restored grid;
and the selected canonical Racket execution produced the same grid in
`counterexamples/top_left_tile_racket.json`, bound to rule hash `55b239af8777`
and generator SHA-256 `cda17d37aca36d09fee0d424e3d959f19048f7c5f65e15637fc4d73fd20a835f`.
The rival output is retained beside it in `top_left_tile_rival.json`.

Yes. Every default profile emitted by the repaired generator overlaps the
missing rectangle with the top-left period block, so every generated input is a
counterexample to this shortcut. The 200-draw-per-band contract probe observed
800/800 such witnesses; the 300-lesson census refuted the shortcut in every
ordered lesson and every one of 1,200 query rotations.
